title: SWPC 27-day outlooks gave no clear added daily storm probability skill beyond a recurrence model in 2018-2025
abstract: We tested whether issued NOAA SWPC 27-day outlook values add daily storm probability skill beyond solar rotation, recent activity, solar flux and season. We fit fixed logistic models on 2010-2017 and tested forecast days 8-27 in 2018-2025. The written-plan sample gave 1,900 test days from 95 issues. For daily NOAA estimated planetary K of at least 5, adding the outlook reduced Brier error by 3.10%, with a conditional 95% four-issue block interval from -1.07% to +7.55%. Brier errors were 0.088586 for recurrence, 0.088629 for the outlook-only model and 0.085839 for the combined model. A post-result check applied the same frozen fits to 7,980 forecasts on 2,913 target dates. With equal date weights, the gain was 2.23% (-0.76% to +5.54%) under 112-day blocks. Final GFZ Kp and rounded thresholds gave small positive point gains, but all four full-archive intervals included zero. Issued Kp of at least 5 marked 96 sampled cases; 34 reached the strict NOAA event. These are numerical guidance values, not issued probabilities. The package gives 21,168 extracted forecast rows, source hashes, joined NOAA cases, frozen models, code, uncertainty draws and figures. Missing archive weeks, revised inputs, one model class, fixed-fit intervals and eight test years limit inference. The study does not show zero information or identify a physical cause of errors.
